input.quote: 9.5 Termination of one Order Form does not terminate another Order Form unless Customer states that the affected Services are operationally inseparable. A termination right is in addition to, and does not exclude, any other remedy available under this Agreement or Applicable Law.
input.rationale: Section 9 provides termination only for material breach (9.1), insolvency (9.2), and Vendor security/SLA/legal/IP failures (9.3); there is no numbered 9.4 and no termination-for-convenience right anywhere in the Agreement (search for "convenience" returns only the Order Form definition). Because Section 8.1 commits Customer to a three-year term (with 12-month Order Form renewals under 8.2), the absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation under the rule's missing-behaviour guidance. We propose new Section 9.4 giving Customer a 30-day convenience right without penalty, keyed to the prepaid-fee refund mechanics in Section 10.2, and confirming Vendor has no reciprocal convenience right during a term.

ops.text: 9.4 Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, without penalty, early-termination charge, or acceleration of Fees. In that case Vendor shall refund prepaid Fees covering the period after the effective date of termination in accordance with Section 10.2. Vendor has no right to terminate this Agreement or an Order Form for convenience during a term.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have added a Customer termination-for-convenience right on 30 days' notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees, since this Agreement runs for a three-year term and Section 9 currently allows exit only for cause, insolvency, or security/SLA failures. Our playbook requires flexibility to exit without penalty; if helpful we can move to 60 days' notice as a fallback.
proposal.summary: Add Section 9.4 giving Customer a 30-day convenience termination right with pro-rata refund and confirming Vendor has none.
